rubric_items.reason: All six design components, including the changed GET /api/patients endpoint (through patientsRouter), have at least one threat.
Most threats are specific (SQL in the subquery, SELECT widening, per-row subquery cost). T-10 elevation of privilege and T-6 repudiation are fairly generic for a read-only change.
Mitigations are either cited existing controls or labelled new controls. T-9 uses the server log rule, which covers request bodies, as a control for client-side logging of response bodies.
Known and assumed are split clearly. Every assumed item is marked as a new control, and the MVP exposure gap is raised as U-1/Q-01 with options and a default.
Readable and consistent between the frontmatter and the body, but threats are ordered by component, not by risk.

findings.text: T-9 uses the logging rule as an existing control for client-side logging. The cited rule comes from the API errorHandler and covers request bodies, while the threat is about logging list response bodies in the web client.

cites.quote: logs carry method, route and error message only, never request bodies; no new logging is added

findings.suggested_fix: Mark T-9's mitigation as a new control for implement (no logging of list responses in web/src/api/client.ts or PatientsPage), or cite a web-side logging rule if one exists.

findings.text: Threats are listed by component, not by risk. The spoofing/MVP exposure (T-5) and the medical-history disclosure (T-2) appear after lower-risk items.

cites.quote: T-1, PatientRepo list query, tampering: request input could alter the new subquery's SQL.

findings.suggested_fix: Order the Threats section by risk, with T-5 and T-2 first.

findings.text: T-5 lists identify and requirePermission as existing controls, but the cited identity section says every MVP permission is granted. They give no protection today; the mitigation is really risk acceptance.

cites.quote: Existing control: requests pass through identify and the route calls requirePermission, which sign-in will replace
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.

findings.suggested_fix: Say that T-5 has no effective control in the MVP and depends only on accepting the risk in Q-01.

cites.quote: Every API request passes through `identify`, which sets the actor
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.
Medical history leaves the database only for the
`appointment_event` records every change with time and actor.
Lists answer `{ items, page, page_size, total }`, 20 per page.
Logs carry method, route and error message only, never request bodies
The web app talks to the API only through `web/src/api/client.ts`.
